Roofing in Webster, Texas

Webster is a few miles from Galveston Bay but outside the state's windstorm catastrophe area, so the roof rules here differ from those in its bay-side neighbors. Call one free number any hour to reach an independent roofing company that takes Webster calls.

Near the water, outside the windstorm map

Roofing in Webster, TX sits in an unusual spot. The city is in Harris County on the Clear Lake side of greater Houston, close enough to Galveston Bay to feel the same storms, yet it is not part of the state's designated catastrophe area. Two of its neighbors are in it: most of League City, across the line in Galveston County, and Seabrook, the part east of State Highway 146, as one of the five Harris County cities on the state's list.

That single fact changes a lot. A Webster re-roof does not need the Texas Department of Insurance windstorm inspection, and it does not end with a WPI-8 certificate. A Webster home also cannot turn to the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association for wind and hail coverage, because TWIA only insures property inside the designated area. The rules that do apply come from the City of Webster's Building Division and from your own homeowners policy.

Houston Expert Roofers does none of the work. Think of it as a switchboard that costs you nothing. A recorded assistant takes calls at all hours, asks what the roof is doing and where in Webster you are, and connects you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes calls here.

Webster permits and contractor paperwork

The City of Webster's Building Division runs permits through an online portal and keeps a contractor registration process. Here is what that means for a roof job, step by step.

  1. Confirm you are inside the City of Webster. A Webster mailing address is not proof. Your Harris Central Appraisal District record lists the taxing jurisdictions for your property.
  2. Ask whether the job needs a permit. The Building Division can tell you what a re-roof or a repair of your size requires. Ask the roofer the same question and compare the answers.
  3. Check the roofer's paperwork with the city. Webster's contractor registration form asks specialty contractors for their license, proof of insurance and business details, and says no permit becomes effective until the required license and certificate of insurance are on file. There is no registration fee. Ask the roofer whether its paperwork is on file in Webster.
  4. File online. The city takes permit applications through its online permit portal. The roofer should apply in its own name and give you the permit number.
  5. Keep the record. Hold on to the permit, the contract, the invoice and the shingle warranty registration. A buyer or an insurer may ask for them later.

The city lists 281-338-2925 for help with online permit applications. Rules and forms change, so confirm the current requirement with the Building Division before work starts.

Wind and hail coverage without TWIA

Along the bay, many owners know the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association as the wind and hail insurer of last resort. TWIA says a property must be located in the catastrophe area designated by the commissioner of insurance to be eligible. In Harris County that area covers only parts of Shoreacres, Seabrook, Pasadena, Morgan's Point and La Porte, inside city limits and east of State Highway 146. Webster is not on that list.

So for a Webster home, wind and hail damage is a question for your regular homeowners policy. Before a storm, ask your agent three things: whether wind and hail carry their own deductible, whether that deductible is a percentage of the home's insured value or a flat amount, and whether the roof is covered at replacement cost or actual cash value. Those answers decide what a roof claim looks like long before any roofer arrives.

After a storm, call the insurer first and let the adjuster see the damage before permanent repairs. A roofer can photograph the roof and explain what it found, but you file the claim.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

What recent storms mean for Webster roofs

Being outside the windstorm map does not mean being out of the wind. Hurricane Beryl made landfall near Matagorda on July 8, 2024, and as it moved inland Community Impact reported over 2.2 million CenterPoint Energy customers in the dark across the region. In May of that year, the National Weather Service office in League City recorded a derecho with winds above 100 mph cutting through parts of the metro. Shingles that lost their seal in either event can look normal from the parking lot and still leak in the next sideways rain.

Signs worth a call: shingles or pieces of ridge cap in the yard, a new ceiling stain, a drip around a light fixture, or dented metal vents. Many roofers inspect at no charge; confirm that on the call.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to CenterPoint Energy or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

Questions to ask a roofer in Webster

  • Is your contractor paperwork on file with the City of Webster, and will you pull the permit if my job needs one?
  • You know Webster is outside the windstorm catastrophe area. Will the roof still be fastened for high wind, and what nailing pattern and underlayment will you use?
  • For a business roof: is it a low-slope membrane, a coating or metal, and what does each option need for drainage?
  • Can you send your certificate of liability insurance to me directly?
  • What is your price per sheet for decking, and will you show me photos before replacing any?
  • What does your workmanship warranty cover, for how long, in writing?

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

Not sure whether a Webster permit applies, or whether the damage is worth a claim? Call and describe the roof. The roofing company you are put through to looks at it in person and gives you its own written estimate.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Is Webster TX in the windstorm area for roofing?

No. The Texas Windstorm Insurance Association's designated catastrophe area covers the 14 first-tier coastal counties plus parts of five named Harris County cities: Shoreacres, Seabrook, Pasadena, Morgan's Point and La Porte, inside city limits and east of State Highway 146. Webster is in Harris County but is not one of those cities, so a re-roof here does not go through the state windstorm inspection and does not end with a WPI-8.

Does a roofer need a permit to work in Webster?

Ask the City of Webster Building Division before work starts. The city takes permit applications through its online permit portal and keeps a contractor registration form on file. That form says no permit becomes effective until the required license and certificate of insurance are on file with the city. Ask the roofer whether it has filed its paperwork with Webster and whether your job needs a permit, and get the permit number in writing if it does.

Can I get TWIA wind coverage on a house in Webster?

TWIA says a property must be located in the catastrophe area designated by the commissioner of insurance to be eligible, and Webster is not in it. So wind and hail on a Webster home are handled through your regular homeowners policy. Ask your agent how your policy treats wind and hail, whether there is a separate deductible for them, and how that deductible is calculated. The roof insurance claims guide lists more questions.

My mailing address says Webster. Which city's rules apply to my roof?

The ones for the city your property actually sits in. Mailing addresses do not always follow city limits, so a Webster address is not proof the house is inside the City of Webster. Your Harris Central Appraisal District record shows the taxing jurisdictions for the property. If it turns out you are inside the City of Houston, the Houston Permitting Center's residential roofing permit rules apply instead.

Who will come out if I call about a roof in Webster?

An independent, locally owned roofing company that takes calls in Webster. Houston Expert Roofers is a free phone line only: an automated assistant answers, asks about the roof and where you are, and transfers you. The roofing company takes it from there: inspection, quote, work, and its own invoice to you. Companies may pay the line a referral fee.
